title: The Major Scale Recipe
description: One pattern of whole and half steps builds a major scale from any key.

steps.title: One pattern, every key
steps.description:
Every major scale follows the same steps. W is a whole step (2 keys up) and H is a half step (1 key up):

W - W - H - W - W - W - H

Start that pattern on C and you land on nothing but white keys. Start it on G and one black key sneaks in. The pattern stays put. Only the starting note moves.

steps.title: C major
steps.description: Play C up to B and feel the steps as you go: C to D is whole, D to E whole, E to F half, then F to G, G to A and A to B are whole, and B back to C is half.
steps.hint: All white keys from C to B.

steps.title: Why C is all white keys
steps.description:
Walk the pattern from C:

• C, whole step to D (hopping over C#)
• D, whole step to E (over D#)
• E, half step to F (no black key in between)
• F, whole step to G (over F#)
• G, whole step to A (over G#)
• A, whole step to B (over A#)
• B, half step to C (no black key in between)

The two half steps in the pattern line up exactly with the two spots on the keyboard where white keys touch, E-F and B-C. That's the only reason C major needs no black keys.

steps.title: G major
steps.description: Run the same pattern from G: G, A, B, C, D, E... and then the next step from E has to be a whole step. That lands on F#, not F.
steps.hint: E to F is only a half step, but the pattern asks for a whole one there. Go one key further to F#, and F# to G gives you the closing half step.

steps.title: F major
steps.description: Now from F: F, G, A, and then the pattern wants a half step. A to B is a whole step, too far, so B drops to Bb.
steps.hint: F, G, A, Bb, C, D, E. Bb is the black key just left of B.

steps.title: The pattern
steps.description: Which pattern builds a major scale?
